newsitem.title: UKRAINE: New Ukraine currency strengthens in street trade.
newsitem.headline: New Ukraine currency strengthens in street trade.

text.p: Ukraine's new hryvnya currency, now four days old, strengthened to 1.65 to the dollar at street exchange points on Thursday from 1.70 early in the week.

"There was no demand for the dollar yesterday," said a money seller at a Kiev exchange point. Many Ukrainians are rushing to acquire the new currency before the old karbovanets is taken out of circulation by September 16.
The hryvnya, worth 100,000 karbovanets, was unchanged at 1.760 per dollar on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange.
About half of the country's exchange points are still closed, helping push up the price of the hryvnya.
"You can't change money anywhere in the city," grumbled one man.
The central bank said it would shut down exchange points still not working.
The karbovanets is still in evidence in many stores but the hryvnya, introduced on Monday, is becoming more common.
